title: Dashboard
blurb: Your home page and the cards on it.

entries.title: Your dashboard
entries.summary: A set of cards you own. Cards (top right) shows, hides and reorders them, and the layout is saved to your account.
entries.note: A card whose feature is off for the install is hidden, not shown empty.

entries.title: Kitchen health
entries.summary: One score from four signals over the last 30 days: waste, budget, freshness and plan coverage.
entries.note: A signal with nothing to score is left out, never scored zero. The arrow compares with a week ago.

entries.title: Next to cook
entries.summary: The next meals someone actually has to cook, in day and slot order.
entries.note: With batch cooking on, meals the pool already covers are left out. Cook opens cook mode at the batch’s yield.

entries.title: Use it up
entries.summary: What is about to go off, expired first, and the recipes that would use the most of it.

entries.title: What's coming
entries.summary: A fortnight at a glance: green dots for meals, red for expiries, blue for a shopping day. Tap a day for the list.

entries.title: Restock radar
entries.summary: Items that went low or out in the last 30 days, newest first, with a cart button.
entries.note: Planned means a meal in the next fortnight still needs it.

entries.title: My budget
entries.summary: Spend this period against the household budget, plus what is still to buy on open lists.
entries.note: Spend counts ticked lines on finished lists with a price.

entries.title: Price drops
entries.summary: Tracked products at a genuine new low against their own history, never a retailer’s ticket price.
entries.note: An opt-in card. Needs products on.

entries.title: The message of the day
entries.summary: A greeting that stays all day, and under it a tip about something easy to miss.

title: Stock
blurb: Your pantry: items, levels, expiry and Dora’s hunches.

entries.title: Add a stock item
entries.summary: Stock → New item. A name and a level are enough; location, group, essential and expiry can come later.

entries.title: Reading a stock row
entries.summary: The square is the level: green stocked, amber low, red out. A dashed ring means the number might be wrong. A row outline means something needs you. A dimmed row is out but not essential.
entries.note: The outline follows the alert kinds you keep on.

entries.title: Finding things
entries.summary: Search by name, quick chips (Needs attention, Expiring soon, Essential, Open), filters for level, location and group, and a sort.
entries.note: Filters survive leaving and returning, not a reload.

entries.title: Quick actions on a row
entries.summary: Tap the square to set a level. The expiry button offers +1, +7 and +14 days, Clear and Log waste. Seal or open an item, or add it to your list.

entries.title: Doing several at once
entries.summary: Bulk select, or hold a row on a phone: add to a list, move, restock, log waste for one reason, or print QR labels.

entries.title: Essentials and auto-add
entries.summary: An essential is chased as soon as it runs low. With auto-add on, a low or out item lands on your draft list by itself.
entries.note: Nothing is auto-added when you have no draft list, or more than one.

entries.title: Expiry and opened
entries.summary: Set a date from the calendar, push it with +1d, +7d or +14d, or clear it. Marking an item opened asks whether to shorten its expiry.
entries.note: Every change is kept on the History tab.

entries.title: The "Dora thinks…" hint
entries.summary: Dora infers a rough Out, Low or Stocked from your purchases, your buying rhythm and your cooking. She only speaks when she disagrees with what you recorded.
entries.note: Her guess never changes your level. A level you set in the last three days wins outright.

entries.title: Hints on other pages
entries.summary: Three switches put the same opinion on the cookbook (May be short, May be cookable), shopping lists (you may be out of…) and the planner.
entries.note: Off by default. They only ever add a remark.

entries.title: Quick checks
entries.summary: When a list or a planned meal depends on an item Dora is unsure of, she asks one question: Still have rice? Set the level and it goes away.

entries.title: The Buy / Wait / Skip ring
entries.summary: A ring on the cart button: green worth buying now, amber maybe wait, red probably skip. Built from your own prices, pace and waste only.
entries.note: When Dora is not confident she says nothing.

entries.title: The stock item page
entries.summary: Every row is its own editor and saves as you change it. Tabs for Products, Recipes, Substitutes, Scanning, Lists and History.
entries.note: A tab is hidden when the feature behind it is off for the install.

entries.title: Dora’s three cards on an item
entries.summary: Dora thinks (her inferred level), planned meals that need it, and Should I buy it? Each opens to its reasoning.
entries.note: None of them is an alert.

entries.title: Your prices
entries.summary: Your own price record: prices you log plus prices from finished shops. Usually is the median of the last year, shown once there are three.
entries.note: Paying more than usual means 15% over that median. Shelf prices of linked products never count.

entries.title: The price history chart
entries.summary: Your logged prices as a solid line, store offers dashed, your usual price dotted. One unit, one axis.

entries.title: Preferred buys
entries.summary: A note of what you actually buy, with no price or store.
entries.note: An item with a linked product uses that product instead, since it answers the same question with real prices.

entries.title: Nutrition on an item
entries.summary: In complex mode, link the item to a food so recipes using it can total their energy. Suggestions are never saved until you tap Use this.

entries.title: An item’s history
entries.summary: One timeline, newest first: level changes, waste, lists, purchases, cooks and the expiry trail.
entries.note: Each kind keeps its latest 50 and says how many were cut.

entries.title: Substitutes
entries.summary: Items that can stand in for one another, with a note and a ratio. Cook mode offers them when something is low.
entries.note: A swap made in cook mode is temporary. The recipe is untouched.

entries.title: Barcodes
entries.summary: A product’s real EAN or UPC, typed or scanned. One code belongs to one item.
entries.note: Dora never looks the number up online.

entries.title: QR label
entries.summary: Dora’s own printable label for an item. Scanning it opens the item’s page.
entries.how: Print one from the Scanning tab, or a batch under Kitchen setup → QR labels.

entries.title: Scanning with an action
entries.summary: Scan opens the camera on Open item. Switch to Set to a level and walk the pantry marking things.
entries.note: A barcode Dora does not know opens New item prefilled.

entries.title: Exporting your stock
entries.summary: Export → CSV or Print / Save as PDF of exactly the rows shown.

entries.title: Deleting a stock item
entries.summary: Removes the item with its history, prices, substitutes and barcodes.
entries.note: Dora refuses while the item is in a recipe, and names them.

entries.title: How stocktake works
entries.summary: Dora walks you through the items due a check, least certain first. Three parts: agree with what she is sure about, the walk, then items that left the rotation.
entries.how: Still correct · Change level · Skip · Push 3 days · Mute.
entries.note: At the end anything you marked low or out can go on a list in one go.

entries.title: Starter packs
entries.summary: At setup, five packs you tick item by item, plus your own items.
entries.note: Items you already have are skipped, not duplicated.

title: Cookbook
blurb: Recipes: writing them, importing them, cost and nutrition.

entries.title: Add and edit a recipe
entries.summary: Cookbook → New recipe makes a stub. Each block has its own pencil; Save commits them together.

entries.title: Ingredients and the pantry
entries.summary: An ingredient points at a pantry item so Dora knows whether you have it, or stays as plain text.
entries.note: Typing a name the pantry does not have offers to add it.

entries.title: Can I cook this?
entries.summary: Yes, no (with what is missing) or unknown (some rows are not linked to the pantry).
entries.note: Missing means out of stock. A low item still counts as cookable.

entries.title: Three ways to write a method
entries.summary: Free text (each line a step), Structured (steps, sub-steps, links to ingredients and tools, timers) or Photos.
entries.note: Switching never deletes the other modes’ content.

entries.title: Sections
entries.summary: Named groups inside a recipe, like For the sauce, holding ingredients and steps.

entries.title: Import a recipe by pasting
entries.summary: Cookbook → Import. Paste a page’s text and Dora picks out the name, times, servings, ingredients and steps.
entries.how: On Android, share the page to Dora instead.
entries.note: Matching to your pantry is fuzzy. Check the rows.

entries.title: Fix unlinked ingredients in bulk
entries.summary: Every unlinked ingredient grouped by its text, so "1 onion" in nine recipes is linked once.

entries.title: Versions of a recipe
entries.summary: New version copies everything into a sibling named (vN). Versions are equal peers, each with its own pool and favourite.

entries.title: Meals prepared
entries.summary: Cooked portions waiting in the fridge or freezer. Cook mode adds them; past planned days use them.
entries.note: Shown in Batch style, hidden in Fresh.

entries.title: What a recipe costs
entries.summary: An estimate from your own prices, ingredient by ingredient. Rows that cannot be priced are reported, not guessed.

entries.title: Nutrition: off, simple, complex
entries.summary: Simple: type kcal per serving. Complex: link items to foods and Dora totals energy per serving, with coverage and a Health Star Rating or Nutri-Score.
entries.note: Ratings are estimates. A missing figure flatters them, and the panel says which.

entries.title: Dietary tags
entries.summary: A planning aid for the include and exclude filter. Check the ingredient list when food safety matters.

entries.title: Marking a recipe cooked
entries.summary: Cooking stamps Last cooked today, adds to the pool in batch style, and writes a Used in event on each ingredient’s history.

title: Cook mode
blurb: One step at a time, with a voice if you want one.

entries.title: Cook mode
entries.summary: One step at a time, large enough to read from across the kitchen. The step’s ingredients and tools light up; tap the progress bar to jump.
entries.how: Cook on a recipe. Keys: → or space next, ← back, R repeat, Esc exit.

entries.title: Cooking for a different number
entries.summary: The Cooking for pill rescales every quantity for this cook only: whole numbers for things you count, kitchen fractions for the rest.

entries.title: Sous Chef
entries.summary: Dora reads each step as you reach it; Repeat reads it again. Her own voice when it is installed on the server, your device’s otherwise.
entries.note: On a phone, a step read after a long silence may be muted by the browser.

entries.title: Hands-free commands
entries.summary: Mic on, then say next, back, repeat, ingredients, tools, start, pause or reset timer, stop, or exit.
entries.note: Chrome, Edge and Safari. Firefox has no speech recognition.

entries.title: Step timers
entries.summary: A step’s own timer, or one Dora reads out of its wording. At zero: a toast, a chime and, with Sous Chef on, a spoken Timer finished.
entries.note: One timer at a time. Moving to another step resets it.

entries.title: Swapping an ingredient
entries.summary: When something is low or out, pick a recorded substitute with its ratio and note.
entries.note: Temporary. The recipe is untouched.

entries.title: Finishing a cook
entries.summary: Each ingredient with its level preselected; change the ones you used up. Last cooked moves to today.
entries.note: Batch households also say how many spare servings went in the pool.

entries.title: The screen stays on
entries.summary: In Cook mode and in a shop the phone does not lock.
entries.note: Needs a browser with wake lock and HTTPS. Elsewhere it locks as usual.

title: Meal plans
blurb: A week at a time, with Dora’s help if you want it.

entries.title: Plan a week
entries.summary: Monday to Sunday with your meal slots on each day. Tap a slot, then a recipe in the rail. Tap the same recipe again to add a serving.
entries.note: Past days are read-only.

entries.title: Build my week
entries.summary: Dora proposes a week from light guidance: days, meals, an emphasis, servings and optionally a budget cap. Edit it before saving.
entries.note: Each meal uses a distinct recipe, so a small cookbook leaves gaps.

entries.title: Dora suggests
entries.summary: The rail’s first chip ranks your cookbook for the week: expiring stock, cookable now, not had lately, favourites, with the reason beside each row.

entries.title: Cook once for several days
entries.summary: Link one recipe across days. The earliest day is the cook day and carries the whole yield; later days are leftovers.
entries.note: Batch style only. Cost is counted once, on the cook day.

entries.title: Cooked fresh on the day
entries.summary: Marks a meal as cooked on its day, outside the pool. It shows a Fresh chip and never takes a ready serving.

entries.title: What the meal glyphs mean
entries.summary: Chef hat: can you make it (green yes, amber missing ingredients). Fridge: is a serving ready (batch only). The card’s edge rolls them up.

entries.title: Templates and rotating sets
entries.summary: Save a week as a template and apply it to one week or a run of weeks. A set rotates templates week by week.
entries.note: Applying replaces the week’s future meals and asks first.

entries.title: Reconcile past meals
entries.summary: As days pass Dora records what happened to each meal. Auto assumes you cooked it and logs it; manual asks you: Cooked, Different portions, Cooked later, Didn’t cook, Skip.
entries.note: Every decision is a new receipt. Nothing is overwritten.

entries.title: Missing this week
entries.summary: The rail totals the week’s ingredients, splits them into out, low and stocked, and hands the missing ones to a shopping list.

entries.title: Cost this week and the budget
entries.summary: Each meal’s price is its recipe estimate times servings. The week’s total sits under the rail against the budget, with cheaper swaps when it is over.

entries.title: Find a lighter option
entries.summary: From a meal’s menu: recipes with fewer kcal per serving and the saving. Never volunteered.

entries.title: Tomorrow at a glance
entries.summary: One evening notification naming tomorrow’s meals and any shopping day. Silent when there is nothing to say.

title: Shopping lists
blurb: From a draft to the shop to the receipt.

entries.title: One list, three faces
entries.summary: A draft while you build it, a shop while you are in the store, a receipt once you finish. Shop starts the trip; Finish ends it.
entries.note: Finishing is final. Ticked items restock when you finish, never before.

entries.title: Which list does the cart button use?
entries.summary: Your only draft. With two or more drafts it asks once and remembers for the tab; with none it asks you to create one.
entries.note: There is no primary list. Shop day is what orders the rail.

entries.title: Adding items
entries.summary: Add item searches every stock item, frequent ones first. The cart button on stock rows, ingredients and products adds with one tap. Add to a list pre-ticks what is missing.
entries.note: A new line remembers your last choice for that item.

entries.title: Start a list from stock, a recipe or a plan
entries.summary: New list fills from low or out items, essentials, frequent buys, a recipe, a plan week or a template.
entries.note: Nothing is added twice.

entries.title: Picking which one
entries.summary: The item’s name on a row is a menu of its linked products’ offers, or its preferred buys when it has no linked product. Picking an offer moves the line to that store.

entries.title: What a line is expected to cost
entries.summary: Estimate: your entered price, else the picked offer, else what you last paid. Store: where you bought it, else the list’s store, else the item’s usual store.

entries.title: Entering prices as you shop
entries.summary: Tap a row’s price to record what you paid, how many and where. Log price records a shelf price for something not on the list.
entries.note: Only entered prices become spend and history.

entries.title: Finish and restock
entries.summary: Ticked items go to Stocked, priced lines become purchase history, names are frozen. Unticked items go to another list or the bin.

entries.title: Amend a receipt
entries.summary: On a finished list, correct price, store and quantity per line. The purchase record is rewritten, so a typo stops feeding estimates.

entries.title: Keep a shop under budget
entries.summary: Over budget, Dora offers to set lines aside, each with its reason. Keep protects a line; Add back restores it.
entries.note: Essentials and meals in the next two days are never cut.

entries.title: Templates
entries.summary: Save a list as a template and start new lists from it in one tap.

entries.title: Receipt photos
entries.summary: Attach up to 20 photos to a shop or a receipt.
entries.note: Record-keeping only. Nothing is read from the image.

entries.title: You may be out of…
entries.summary: On a draft, a strip of items Dora thinks you have run out of that are not on the list yet. Tap to add.
entries.note: Nothing is added for you.

title: Products and prices
blurb: Saved products, price history and deals.

entries.title: What a product is
entries.summary: One thing at one shop with a price. A stock item is the thing in your kitchen. Link them and the price rides with your pantry record.

entries.title: Finding products
entries.summary: Product Search opens the page your admin set up. What you save there lands in My products.
entries.note: No Product Search in the menu? Your admin sets it up under Admin → Product data.

entries.title: Link or unlink a product
entries.summary: Grey broken link means not linked: tap to pick a stock item. Green means linked: tap to unlink.

entries.title: Custom products
entries.summary: For a shop Dora cannot check. You type the price, size and store; Dora never refreshes it and marks it Custom.

entries.title: Items in the pack
entries.summary: Set how many are in a pack so a recipe’s 3 eggs can be priced.

entries.title: Tracking prices
entries.summary: Stop tracking hides a product from deals and the weekly email without deleting it.
entries.note: On a product you added yourself the menu says Hide from deals, since nothing refreshes its price.

entries.title: Bulk select
entries.summary: All visible, On deal, Low stock on deal and more. Then add to a list, unlink, stop tracking or delete in one go.

entries.title: Watch a price
entries.summary: From a product’s menu, Alert me on a price drop. A new offer at or below your figure raises a bell alert, once per offer.
entries.note: Price alerts need money features on.

entries.title: Price history
entries.summary: Compare up to five products over 30 days, 90 days, a year or all time, with your usual price where you have logged one.

entries.title: Weekly deals email
entries.summary: Pick a day under Notifications; the mail arrives at 7 am with the best specials across your tracked products.
entries.note: A quiet week sends nothing. Needs a verified email address.

entries.title: Is it really a deal?
entries.summary: Dora checks a special against the product’s own 90-day history and what you have paid. A special dearer than your usual price is called out.

entries.title: Deleting a product
entries.summary: Gone for good, with its price history and any watch on it.
entries.note: Finished lists keep their record of it.

title: Alerts and notifications
blurb: The bell, push, and Dora’s suggestions.

entries.title: The bell
entries.summary: Counts the actionable things: expired food, an essential low or out, expiring soon, a missed shop, a price hit. Lower-key nudges are listed, not counted.

entries.title: What each alert means
entries.summary: Expired · Expiring soon · Essential low or out · Did you forget your shopping? · Shopping day · No meals planned · Past meals need confirming · Hit your price.
entries.note: A non-essential running low is not an alert. The stock row already says it.

entries.title: Snooze, dismiss, and why alerts come back
entries.summary: Each alert is one episode. Dismiss hides it until that episode ends; Snooze hides it for seven days. The next pack of apples is a new alert.

entries.title: Choosing which alerts you get
entries.summary: A switch per kind, for you only. Off removes it from the bell, the stock rows and push.

entries.title: Push notifications
entries.summary: Needs push keys from an admin, a browser that supports push, and the switch on for this device. Dora pushes new actionable alerts hourly, once each.
entries.note: On an iPhone, add Dora to the home screen first.

entries.title: The evening brief
entries.summary: 7 pm in your household’s timezone: tomorrow’s meals and any shopping day due. Rides push and sends nothing on an empty evening.

entries.title: Dora’s suggestions
entries.summary: Ideas, not alerts: use something soon, over budget, probably due, buy less, still have it?, meals to confirm. Cards at the top of her chat with Why?, Snooze and Dismiss.
entries.note: Dismissing hides a suggestion for the whole household.

entries.title: What Reports is built from
entries.summary: Your own records: finished lists with prices, cooks logged in cook mode, logged prices and marked waste. Nothing is looked up.

entries.title: The range and All time
entries.summary: Every card answers for the range you pick. All time starts at your first record; waste looks back at most a year.

entries.title: Where the money went
entries.summary: By store, by stock group, or against the same-length period before.
entries.note: Items with no price are counted and named, never silently dropped.

entries.title: Kitchen memory
entries.summary: Cooks finished in cook mode, the portions you made, and how many different recipes that was.

entries.title: Price changes
entries.summary: First and last price in the range for items with two or more logged prices, per shelf unit. Tap an item for its chart.

entries.title: Logging waste
entries.summary: On a stock row, open the expiry menu, Mark as wasted, then a reason. Undo within five seconds puts it back.

entries.title: The household budget
entries.summary: One amount, weekly from Monday or monthly. Spent is ticked lines on finished lists; projected is what is on open lists dated in the period.

entries.title: Reports with money off
entries.summary: Waste and Kitchen memory stay. Summary, Spend and Price changes go.

title: Dora
blurb: The assistant in the corner, and what she can do.

entries.title: Basic or AI
entries.summary: Basic is always on and works offline: lookups, conversions, substitutes, adding to your list, page help. AI understands looser phrasing and needs a provider you connect.
entries.note: If AI drops out mid-chat, Dora answers in Basic for that message.

entries.title: What you can ask
entries.summary: How’s my pantry · what’s low · what’s expiring · where’s the milk · what’s for dinner · recipe for carbonara · what’s on my list · 1 cup to ml · substitute for butter · what can I do here.

entries.title: Adding to your list by chat
entries.summary: Type add milk and eggs. Dora matches the names against your pantry and adds the clear ones to your draft list.
entries.note: Anything ambiguous she asks about, never guesses.

entries.title: Dora never changes anything on her own
entries.summary: In AI mode every change arrives as a card you Confirm or Cancel. Until you tap Confirm, nothing has happened.

entries.title: What Dora can see
entries.summary: Your household’s data in this install. Never another household, never the web.
entries.note: With OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini your messages go to that provider. Ollama keeps everything on your own machine.

entries.title: Set up AI mode
entries.summary: Ollama (a local model, no key) or OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini (your own key). Test connection before turning it on. Per account.

entries.title: Why does AI mode say unavailable?
entries.summary: The provider did not answer: Ollama is not running, the key is wrong, the model is mistyped, or the server cannot reach the URL.
entries.note: The URL is from the server’s point of view, not your browser’s. Retry on the banner after fixing it.

entries.title: Paid providers need an encryption key
entries.summary: The install needs DORA_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY set so your API key is stored encrypted. The Assistant page says so and can generate one.
entries.note: Rotating the key invalidates every saved key.

entries.title: Talking to Dora
entries.summary: Tap the mic, speak, tap again. Your words land in the box so you can read them before sending.
entries.note: Chrome and Edge. Firefox has no speech recognition.

entries.title: Hearing Dora
entries.summary: The speaker button has Dora read her replies aloud, with her own voice when it is installed on the server.

entries.title: Which browsers can Dora speak in?
entries.summary: All of them, with her own voice installed on the server. The browser’s voice is the part that varies, and Firefox often has none.

entries.title: How does Dora know what page I’m on?
entries.summary: She reads the route. Ask what can I do here on any page.

entries.title: Suggestions in the chat
entries.summary: The number on the launcher is how many suggestions Dora has. Open the chat to Accept, Snooze a day, Dismiss, or ask Why.

entries.title: Why does Dora say slow down?
entries.summary: Twenty questions a minute per person is the ceiling, so a stuck script cannot run up your provider bill. She answers in Basic until the minute is up.

entries.title: Turning Dora off
entries.summary: Show digital assistant chat bubble, off. Hides the launcher everywhere for your account only.

entries.title: Her faces
entries.summary: The burger in the corner reacts to the conversation.

title: Getting started
blurb: First run, signing in and your account.

entries.title: Your first run
entries.summary: A short story, then a one-minute setup. Nothing is saved until Finish.
entries.note: Skip keeps the defaults, and the dashboard offers to continue for a day.

entries.title: What Finish sets up
entries.summary: Your look; for the first user also the household, the feature switches, starter items and optionally one demo recipe.
entries.note: Everything is editable afterwards in Stock and Settings.

entries.title: Running setup again
entries.summary: Settings → About → Welcome tour starts it over.

entries.title: Signing in and creating an account
entries.summary: A username and password. An admin adds new people on Settings → Users. If the admin has switched on sign-ups there, the sign-in page also offers "Need an account?". Passwords are 8 or more characters, and new accounts are never admins.
entries.note: A failed sign-in never says which half was wrong.

entries.title: The first admin
entries.summary: A brand-new install opens on a one-time page that creates the first admin and signs them in. Then the page is gone for good.

entries.title: Forgot your password
entries.summary: Enter your email; if it is on an account a one-hour reset link arrives.
entries.note: The button appears only when the install can send email. Otherwise an admin sets a new password for you.

entries.title: Verifying your email
entries.summary: Accounts with an address get a 24-hour link. Scheduled emails only go to verified addresses.

entries.title: Why was I signed out?
entries.summary: A password change or reset signs out your other devices. An admin deactivating an account signs it out. Cleared cookies end a session.

entries.title: The phone app and your Dora address
entries.summary: The app asks for your server’s address once and adds /api for you.
entries.how: Change it later under Settings → About.

entries.title: Username, email and password
entries.summary: Edit them inline under Account and Save.
entries.note: Changing your password signs out your other devices.

entries.title: Profile picture
entries.summary: Upload a photo or pick a preset. It saves the moment you choose.

title: Settings and admin
blurb: Your preferences, the kitchen setup, and the install.

entries.title: Settings and Admin
entries.summary: Personal settings and install-wide Admin settings are two modes. Admins switch with the pill at the top.
entries.note: Kitchen setup is shared by the household even though it sits on the personal side.

entries.title: Who can change what
entries.summary: Anyone edits their own account, appearance, notifications, voice and the shared kitchen setup. Only admins change install-wide behaviour.

entries.title: Appearance
entries.summary: Mode (System, Light, Dark), a theme family, a font and one of four text sizes. Per account, and it follows you across devices.
entries.note: The sign-in page is always the light brand look.

entries.title: Notifications
entries.summary: Which alert kinds reach your bell, how long alerts live, push for this device, the evening brief and the weekly deals email.

entries.title: Voice
entries.summary: Speak to Dora, and let her speak back with her own voice or your device’s.
entries.note: Her voices are 60 to 110 MB downloads on the server.

entries.title: Stock locations
entries.summary: A three-level map of where things live: zones, areas, sections. Items can sit at any level.
entries.note: Deleting a zone leaves its items unassigned, not deleted.

entries.title: Stock groups and recipe vocabulary
entries.summary: Name-only lists used as filters and pickers, each showing how many things use it.
entries.note: Meal slots are the one reorderable list, and their order drives the planner.

entries.title: Stores
entries.summary: The shops Dora knows about. Add one, give it a logo, remove the ones you do not use.

entries.title: How Dora shows dates, money and units
entries.summary: Every date, price and unit follows the household’s region, not your browser.

entries.title: Keyboard shortcuts
entries.summary: Press ? anywhere for the list. / focuses search; g then s, l, r, d or h jumps to Stock, Lists, Cookbook, Dashboard or Help.
entries.note: Shortcuts never use Ctrl or Cmd, so they cannot collide with the browser’s.

entries.title: Region and locale (admin)
entries.summary: Currency, language, units and the household timezone. Match this device fills zone, locale and units.
entries.note: The timezone decides which day is today everywhere.

entries.title: Kitchen features (admin)
entries.summary: One page per switch: stock auto-add and scanning, stocktake, cooking style, meal reconciliation, money, nutrition, alert thresholds, image quality.
entries.note: Each flip is install-wide and applies to everyone on their next page load.

entries.title: Email and push setup (admin)
entries.summary: SMTP details, the email switch, the public URL used in links, and the keys for web push.
entries.note: Secrets are stored encrypted and need DORA_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY on the server.

entries.title: Manage users (admin)
entries.summary: Add, rename, reset passwords, promote, deactivate (locks them out, keeps everything) or delete.
entries.note: You cannot demote or remove yourself, or the last admin who can still sign in.

entries.title: Audit log (admin)
entries.summary: Every change, sign-in attempt and client crash, filterable, with CSV export.
entries.note: Retention is 1 to 3650 days, pruned nightly.

title: Data and access
blurb: Backups, imports and API keys. Admins only.

entries.title: Back up your install
entries.summary: Everything Dora knows, saved to one file in the Backup library on the server. Download any of them to keep a copy elsewhere.
entries.note: Passwords and secrets are never included. Backups are manual.

entries.title: Restore a backup
entries.summary: Brings rows in. Rows that already exist are skipped, never overwritten. From a file you first see a preview and pick exactly what to bring.
entries.note: Restore adds, it does not delete. Reload afterwards.

entries.title: Import stock items from a spreadsheet
entries.summary: An .xlsx or .csv with at least a name column. Download the template, fill it, check the column mapping, import.
entries.note: Levels must already exist. Locations and groups can be created on the fly.

entries.title: Create an API key
entries.summary: Lets a program you run push products and prices into Dora. The key is shown once, right after you create it.
entries.note: Anyone holding the key can change products in this install. Lose it, revoke it and make a new one.

entries.title: Map the store names a source uses
entries.summary: An unknown store name holds the record as pending under that key until you say which of your stores it means.
entries.note: Records pushed before you map are not queued. The source pushes them again.

entries.title: See whether a source is working
entries.summary: Each key shows when it was last used and running totals of records accepted, skipped and failed.

entries.title: Disable or revoke a key
entries.summary: Disable pauses a source and keeps its mappings. Revoke deletes the key for good.
entries.note: Neither removes the products already pushed.

title: Offline, install and updates
blurb: Dora on your devices, and where your data lives.

entries.title: Use Dora when the connection drops
entries.summary: A red strip appears and you can keep looking at anything you have opened before. Changes wait until you are back.
entries.note: Dora never saves a change for later, so what you see is always what the server has.

entries.title: Install Dora on your phone or computer
entries.summary: Settings → About → Install as an app. On an iPhone, Share → Add to Home Screen.
entries.note: Needs HTTPS. Installing does not change your data or sign you in anywhere new.

entries.title: A new version is ready
entries.summary: After the server is updated a blue strip appears. Reload when convenient.
entries.note: The yellow notice on About is about the server itself, for whoever runs it.

entries.title: The Android app
entries.summary: The same Dora in a native wrapper. It asks for your server’s address on first launch.
entries.note: Push is not available inside the Android app. Use the installed web app for that.

entries.title: Where Dora keeps your data
entries.summary: On the server: the dora_data volume on Docker, or your app-data folder with the desktop app. Never in the browser.
entries.note: Deleting that folder deletes the install. Take a backup first.

entries.title: Is there a newer Dora?
entries.summary: Help → About shows the version you run and whether a newer release exists. Updating is the operator’s job.

entries.title: Why does a banner say Demo mode?
entries.summary: The install was started as a public demo. Sample data, and everything resets on a timer.
entries.note: Nothing you change is kept.

entries.title: Something went wrong, and the ref code
entries.summary: A short code like ref: 3f9a2c1b on an error is the id of that request in the server log. Quote it when you report a problem.

entries.title: Reporting a problem
entries.summary: Help → About → Report an issue, when the operator has set one up. Otherwise note the steps and pass them on.
